events.text: Mount Hua's roof leaks again, the rice jar is half empty, and the Sect Leader is pretending not to notice. The disciples are hungry and proud about it.

choices.text: Take escort work to feed the sect

effects.log: Three months of caravans. The rice jar is full. The Sect Leader pretends not to notice that too, and squeezes your shoulder.
You leave a purse on the kitchen table without a word. That night there is meat in the soup for the first time in a year.
The plum trees bloom whether the sect is rich or not. So will you.

events.text: Snow on the peak, and the plum trees blooming through it. Watching a petal fall, you suddenly understand why the Plum Blossom Sword moves the way it does.

choices.text: Sit under the tree until it is clear

ok.log: When you rise, your sword blooms like the tree. The elders who see it go very quiet.

fail.log: You sit in the snow until you can no longer feel your legs. Almost. Next winter, perhaps.

choices.text: Draw your sword now, before it fades

effects.log: Seven petals of sword qi, one after another. Not perfect. But yours.

events.text: A Namgung heir sneers at Mount Hua in the teahouse: 'a poor sect with a pretty sword'. Every Mount Hua disciple in the room turns to look at you.

ok.log: The Namgung heir leaves with a torn sleeve and a lesson. Mount Hua drinks for free that night.

fail.log: The Namgung sword is as good as its reputation. You will be back.

effects.log: 'Pretty, and poor. Both true.' The room laughs with you, and the heir looks foolish instead.

events.text: The Abbot summons you. Word has reached the temple: you took a life. Shaolin's first rule is not a suggestion.

choices.text: Repent: ten years of meditation and sutras

effects.log: Ten years facing a wall. You come out quieter, clearer, and stronger in ways the Abbot said you would be.

ok.log: The Abbot listens a long time. 'Then carry it,' he says. 'Every day.' You are not expelled.

fail.log: The temple gate closes behind you. The monks do not watch you go, which is worse.

effects.log: You leave your robe folded on the steps. Some doors you close yourself.

events.text: The Hall of Bronze Men: eighteen monks in bronze-lacquered skin guard the gate. Pass through, and Shaolin's secret arts open to you.

ok.log: You come out the other side bruised from crown to heel. The Abbot himself is waiting with a scroll.

fail.log: The eighteenth Bronze Man sends you back through the door you came in. Next year.

effects.log: The Bronze Men will be there next year. They are always there.

events.text: An old Wudang master pushes you with one finger and you fall over. 'You meet force with force,' he says. 'Water does not.'

ok.log: A season of pushing hands. At the end, he pushes you and you flow. He smiles for the first time.

fail.log: You fall over for a whole season. It is humbling. Next season, maybe.

effects.log: He sighs, steps aside, and you fall over again. Some lessons take longer.

events.text: Shaolin and Wudang hold their once-in-a-decade debate: whose way is closer to the truth. You are chosen to speak for your sect.

ok.log: Even the other side nods. The debate ends in tea, which is the best way debates end.

fail.log: You lose the thread halfway. The other sect is gracious about it, which somehow makes it worse.

ok.log: Words are wind; fists are honest. Both sects enjoy it far more than the debate.

fail.log: The other side's champion is very honest with their fists.

events.text: Every Tang child is fed a little poison each year, so no poison can kill them later. This year it is your turn for a stronger dose.

ok.log: A night of fever and strange dreams. In the morning, you are a true Tang: poison is just a spice now.

fail.log: It nearly kills you. The elders nod approvingly. 'Next year,' they say.

effects.log: The elders say nothing. Tang elders say nothing very loudly.

events.text: A cousin is selling the recipe of the Tang soul-taking needle to the Hushed Lantern Pavilion. You have the proof.

choices.text: Take it to the family head

effects.log: The cousin disappears from the family records, and from Sichuan. The family head gives you a key to a cabinet you did not know existed.

ok.log: You meet the buyers at the river. The recipe never leaves Sichuan, and neither do the buyers.

fail.deathCause: Hushed Lantern assassins at the river
fail.log: The buyers were assassins. Of course they were.

events.text: A beggar with a knotted cloth hands you a message: the Beggars' Sect knows where a wanted Blood Cult elder is hiding. Someone has to act on it.

ok.log: The elder is taken alive. The whole sect hears who did it.

fail.log: The elder escapes, and you barely do.

choices.text: Sell the information to the Alliance

effects.log: The Alliance pays well. The Beggars' Sect gets its cut. Everyone eats.

events.text: A captured Orthodox scout kneels before you. The Cult elder watching you says: 'Prove your heart belongs to the Heavenly Demon.'

effects.log: The elder nods. 'Good.' You do not sleep that night, and the next night it is easier. That is the worst part.

ok.log: A knot too loose, a door not quite shut. Nobody can prove anything.

fail.log: The elder can prove it. The punishment is educational.

events.text: A purge sweeps the halls: anyone suspected of doubting is dragged away. Your name is on a list. Someone put it there.

ok.log: The accuser's own name ends up at the top of the list. The purge moves on without you.

fail.log: You survive the questioning. Your trust in anyone here does not.

effects.log: You go over the wall at midnight. The Cult never forgets a deserter.

events.text: The Namgung patriarch reviews the family's young swords. 'The Namgung name is heaven's sword,' he says. 'Show me you deserve it.'

choices.text: Show him the Azure Sky Sword

ok.log: The patriarch watches in silence, then taps the ground with his staff once. That is how the Namgung say 'excellent'.

fail.log: He turns away before you finish. The family will be watching you closely this year.

effects.log: Nobody has asked in thirty years. He is so surprised he actually shows you. You learn more in one breath than in a year.

events.text: Emei's abbess asks every disciple the same question once: 'Will your sword serve the weak, or your own name?'

effects.log: She nods, and from that day you are sent where the need is greatest.
'Honest,' she says. 'Rare. We will work on the rest.'

events.text: On the highest ridge of Kunlun, wind strong enough to throw a horse. The masters cross it without their feet touching the snow.

ok.log: Three steps on nothing, then the other side. The masters say nothing, which at Kunlun is high praise.

fail.log: The wind wins. You catch yourself on a ledge and climb back, very humbly.

effects.log: You watch for a month. You begin to see where they put their weight: nowhere.

events.text: A rival stronghold has taken a toll road that belongs to yours. Your chief looks at you. 'Get it back.'

ok.log: By dawn the road is yours again, and the rival stronghold is short three lieutenants.

fail.deathCause: a turf war over a toll road
fail.log: They were waiting for you. You crawl home.

effects.log: Silver talks. The road is yours again, and nobody bleeds. The chief grumbles, but pays you back.

choices.text: Tell the chief the road is not worth your blood

effects.log: The chief looks at you for a long time, then gives the job to someone else. The road stays lost, and your name slides down the hall's list.

events.text: Your first real contract arrives in a sealed envelope. The target is a corrupt magistrate who has ruined a hundred families.

ok.log: In and out before the night watch changes. The hundred families never know who to thank.

fail.log: The magistrate's guards are awake. You escape through the kitchen, empty-handed.

effects.log: The sect does not like refusals. They will remember. So will you.

events.text: The Jegal elders set every young member the same test: walk out of the Stone Maze of Eight Gates before the incense stick burns down.

ok.log: You walk out with half the stick left. The elder in charge of the maze moves one stone, thoughtfully, so it will be harder next year.

fail.log: The incense burns out while you are still admiring a very clever dead end.

ok.log: You are out in a minute. The elders argue for an hour about whether that counts. It counts.

fail.log: The walls are part of the formation. You fall back into the maze from the top, into a very undignified heap.

events.text: A general sends a sealed letter to the Jegal family: his army is trapped in a valley, and he will listen to exactly one advisor. The family sends you.

ok.log: Fires on the ridges, drums in the wrong valley, and the army walks out at night without losing a man. The general writes the Jegal name on his banner.

fail.log: Half the army gets out. The general is grateful and grim. The family is quiet with you for a while.

choices.text: Tell him to surrender with honour

effects.log: Nobody dies. The general never forgives you, and his men never forget you.

events.text: The Paeng family's victory feast: three days of roast meat, sabre dances and shouting. Tradition says the youngest member must out-eat an elder.

ok.log: The elder puts down the chopsticks on the second night. The whole family carries you around the courtyard on a shield.

fail.log: You fall asleep on the roof on the fourth day, too full to climb down. Nobody will tell you how you got there. Everyone is very proud of you anyway.

choices.text: Challenge the elder to a sabre dance instead

ok.log: Your sabre sings. The elder laughs so hard he forgets to drink. The Paeng love a good loud answer.

fail.log: The elder's sabre sings louder. You still get a bowl of stew for trying.

events.text: Northern raiders cross the river at night. The Paeng family rides out, as it always has, loud and first.

ok.log: By dawn the raiders are back across the river. The family head gives you his own sabre to hold at the victory feast.

fail.log: The raiders are stronger this year. You come home on a stretcher, still shouting.

choices.text: Guard the villages behind the river

effects.log: No songs about you this time. The villages are still standing, which is the point.

events.text: White Crane Mountain has twelve disciples, one master and a roof that leaks onto the master's bed every time it rains.

effects.log: Three days on the roof in the wind. The master sleeps dry for the first time in years and pretends it was always like this.

choices.text: Hunt pelts to pay for tiles

ok.log: New tiles, and meat for the whole sect. Small sects remember small miracles.

fail.log: The mountain wins this time. You come back with one pelt and a limp.

events.text: A great sect offers to absorb White Crane Mountain: a new roof, full rice jars, and the end of its name. The master asks what you think.

ok.log: You turn the envoys away with a bow and a promise. The next year, twenty new disciples climb the mountain because they heard the story.

fail.log: The sect stays itself, and stays poor. Nobody regrets it out loud.

choices.text: "Take the offer. The disciples need to eat."

effects.log: The rice jars fill. The old name is carved on a stone by the gate, so it is not forgotten.
